intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh-squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the towering golden dunes of the Sahara at sunset and spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a canopy of stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine, mint tea, and live Gnawa music. Wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Historic Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit the Medersa Ben Youssef, the 14th-century Saadian Tombs, and the Bahia Palace. Explore the spice souks, leather tanneries, and artisan workshops that have operated for centuries.

experiences.name: Moroccan Cooking Class in a Riad
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class hosted inside a traditional riad courtyard. Learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as chicken tagine with preserved lemon, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla. Visit the local market beforehand to select fresh spices and ingredients with your host chef.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Strap on a sandboard and carve down the steep, silky slopes of the Erg Chebbi mega-dunes for an adrenaline-packed desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction for all skill levels. Combine with quad biking across the desert flats for an extra thrill at minimal additional cost.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a petit taxi or pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Negotiate taxi fare in advance (expect ~70–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from a 24-hour convenience store or airport kiosk upon arrival — budget ~20–30 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) exchanged at the airport for taxi and immediate expenses. Avoid unlicensed touts at the airport. Confirm hotel address in Arabic if possible to show the taxi driver.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, head to Djemaa el-Fna Square — the beating heart of Marrakech. Explore the iconic open square, watch street performers, snake charmers, and acrobats. Stroll through the surrounding souks (markets) in the medina. Visit the spice market and leather goods stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Koutoubia Mosque (exterior view — non-Muslims cannot enter) and admire its stunning 12th-century minaret. Continue to the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully ornate 19th-century palace with intricate tilework and lush gardens. Afterward, wander through the mellah (old Jewish quarter) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset when it transforms into a massive open-air food market. Eat dinner at one of the communal food stalls (stalls 1–100 offer tagines, harira soup, grilled meats, and fresh orange juice). Budget ~60–80 MAD for a full meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with argan oil and honey (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks — a kefta sandwich or bowl of harira soup (~15–25 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — tagine + bread + fresh orange juice (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Dress modestly out of respect for local culture (cover shoulders and knees). Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis only rediscovered in 1917. Then head to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a dramatic open-air ruin with storks nesting on the walls. Both sites are within walking distance in the southern medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to the Mellah Market for fresh local produce, olives, and dried fruits. Visit the Museum of Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace, featuring Moroccan art and artifacts. Spend time in the peaceful courtyard. Alternatively, explore the free Mouassine Fountain area in the medina.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional hammam (public bathhouse) for an authentic local experience. Head to a local hammam like Hammam Dar el-Bacha (budget ~50–80 MAD for basic scrub session). Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner at a local restaurant near the medina.

meals.breakfast: Café Clock or a local café near the medina — café au lait and msemen (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in the medina — couscous Friday special or tagine with bread (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Lamine near Djemaa el-Fna — famous for mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at very affordable prices (~50–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam visit for late afternoon to avoid crowds. Bring a change of clothes and flip-flops. March weather in Marrakech is mild (~18–22°C) — a light jacket for evenings is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) on a shared budget group tour or CTM bus toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dades Gorge. This is typically a 2-day desert excursion. The scenic drive passes through the Atlas Mountains, Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa'), and dramatic kasbahs. Stop at Aït Benhaddou Kasbah (UNESCO World Heritage Site, entry ~10 MAD) — a stunning ancient fortified village used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley with its lush palm oases and traditional mud-brick villages. Stop at Ouarzazate for lunch and a quick visit to the exterior of Atlas Studios (one of the world's largest film studios). Continue toward Zagora or Merzouga (depending on tour route) through the dramatic Saharan landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara Desert near Merzouga or Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount camels for a 1-hour sunset camel trek into the dunes (included in most budget desert tours). Watch the spectacular Sahara sunset over the golden dunes. Arrive at a budget desert camp for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure (~20–30 MAD) or packed snacks
meals.lunch: Roadside local restaurant in Ouarzazate — tagine and bread (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner included at desert camp — traditional Moroccan tagine and bread around a campfire under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book a budget shared desert tour in advance from Marrakech (expect ~400–600 MAD for a 2-day/1-night shared tour including camel ride and camp). Pack warm layers — Sahara nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headscarf for wind and sand. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech as camps have limited electricity.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the breathtaking Sahara sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. Take photos, explore the dunes on foot, and enjoy the silence of the desert. After breakfast at camp, begin the return journey toward Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Todra Gorge — a dramatic canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored rock walls. Walk through the narrow gorge floor along the river (free entry). Great for photography and a short hike. Continue driving back through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) with stunning panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (~7:00–8:00 PM). Check back into the hotel, shower, and relax. Enjoy a calm evening stroll through the Gueliz (modern Marrakech) neighborhood for a change of scenery from the medina.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast included at desert camp — Moroccan mint tea, bread, honey, and eggs
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop near Todra Gorge — sandwiches and local snacks (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Gueliz — try Al Fassia-style Moroccan food or a local grill restaurant (~50–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Merzouga to Marrakech is approximately 9–10 hours with stops. Rest in the vehicle as much as possible. The Tizi n'Tichka pass road can be winding — those prone to motion sickness should sit in the front seat and take medication if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Ourika Valley (~30 km from Marrakech) by shared grand taxi (~30–40 MAD each way from Bab Rob). Enjoy a scenic hike along the river through Berber villages to the Setti Fatma waterfalls. The hike to the first waterfall takes about 20–30 minutes and is moderately easy. Swim in the natural pools if weather permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Berber villages along the valley, visit a local women's argan oil cooperative to learn about traditional argan oil production (free entry, small purchases support local women). Return to Marrakech by mid-afternoon. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~100 MAD) — a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, with the Berber Museum inside.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) at dusk — visit the historic synagogues and the vibrant Mellah market. End the evening back at Djemaa el-Fna for fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD per glass) and people-watching. Catch live Gnawa music performances in the square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — mint tea, msemen, and amlou (almond-argan dip) (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Local Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley — freshly prepared tagine with mountain views (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — grilled brochettes, Moroccan salads, and fresh juice (~50–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Ourika Valley hike — the path near the waterfalls can be slippery. Negotiate the grand taxi price before boarding. The Majorelle Garden can be crowded — arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) or late afternoon for fewer crowds. Photography inside the garden is permitted.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the final morning doing last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — look for budget-friendly items like argan oil, leather goods, Berber jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, and spice mixes. Practice your bargaining skills! Visit the Rahba Kedima (Spice Square) for authentic spices and herbal products at local prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a final leisurely lunch in the medina. Visit any remaining sites — consider a free walk through the Mouassine neighborhood with its beautiful fountains and riads. Pack your bags at the hotel and check out. Arrange a taxi to the airport (negotiate ~70–100 MAD for a petit taxi or use a metered grand taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Marrakech Menara Airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Enjoy one last glass of Moroccan mint tea at the airport café (~15–20 MAD). Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and authentic Moroccan experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a café near the medina — café au lait, croissant, and fresh orange juice (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café des Épices on Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with medina views, affordable Moroccan dishes (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport café or restaurant — budget ~50–80 MAD depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some MAD for taxi and airport expenses but spend remaining cash on souvenirs. Declare any argan oil purchases over 1 liter if traveling to certain countries. Total estimated daily budget excluding tours: ~200–300 MAD/day (~$20–30 USD) for food and local transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer or petit taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Grab a light snack from the hotel if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at layover airport
meals.dinner: Light hotel snack or room service upon arrival — budget around 80–120 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm your hotel transfer in advance to avoid taxi haggling after a long flight. Exchange some cash (MAD) at the airport for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. After breakfast, head to the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square (a 10–20 min taxi ride from most Marrakech hotels). Explore the bustling square in the late morning when it is calmer and less crowded. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful stroll and great photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the labyrinthine Medina souks. Explore the spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather goods souk, and the famous Souk Semmarine. Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) to admire its intricate Moroccan architecture and lush courtyards. Allow 1.5 hours for the palace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms at sunset — watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians. Browse food stalls for a classic Moroccan street dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Café Arabe or a local riad café in the Medina — tagine or harira soup, budget 80–150 MAD
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — grilled meats, merguez, fresh orange juice, budget 60–100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina. Bargaining is expected in souks — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small bag and be mindful of pickpockets in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterwards, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a vast 16th-century palace complex with panoramic views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the vibrant Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for a cultural contrast — visit the historic Lazama Synagogue and browse the gold jewelry souk. In the late afternoon, visit the Maison de la Photographie (entry ~50 MAD) for fascinating historical photographs of Morocco from the 19th and 20th centuries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a hammam experience at a mid-range traditional hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Bain Bleu (budget 250–400 MAD including scrub and massage). End the evening with dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café — msemen (Moroccan pancakes) with honey and argan oil, budget 30–60 MAD
meals.lunch: Restaurant Marrakchi or similar — couscous or pastilla, budget 100–180 MAD
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant or Le Jardin rooftop — modern Moroccan cuisine, budget 150–250 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance, especially for evenings. The Saadian Tombs can have queues — arriving right at opening (9:00 AM) is recommended. Keep your ticket stubs as some sites do spot checks.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a private or shared day-tour transfer heading toward Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley. The journey takes approximately 5–6 hours with scenic stops. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains for breathtaking panoramic views and photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Draa Valley or Zagora region by early afternoon. Stop at the ancient Aït Ben Haddou ksar (UNESCO World Heritage Site, entry ~10 MAD) — a spectacular fortified mud-brick village used as a film set for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ksar with a local guide (optional, ~100–150 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Continue to your desert camp or Zagora area accommodation. Arrive in time for sunset over the dunes. Enjoy a camel ride at sunset (30–45 min, ~150–200 MAD). Settle into a mid-range desert camp with Berber tents for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure or packed breakfast arranged with hotel
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Ouarzazate or Aït Ben Haddou — tagine and bread, budget 80–130 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at desert camp — harira, tagine, mint tea, and live music around the campfire, typically included in camp package

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — bring water, snacks, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the mountain pass (it can be cold even in March). Confirm whether the desert camp is included in your package or book separately (mid-range camps: 600–1,200 MAD/night including dinner and breakfast).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00–6:30 AM) for a magical sunrise over the Sahara dunes — one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Take a guided sunrise walk or camel ride into the dunes. After breakfast at camp, explore the surrounding desert landscape on foot or by quad bike (optional, ~300–400 MAD for 1 hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart camp and head toward Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) if not already there, or begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different scenic route through the Dadès Gorge and Roses Valley. Stop at Skoura Oasis palm grove for a peaceful walk among thousands of palm trees and ancient kasbahs.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Dadès Valley or Boumalne Dadès area for an overnight stop (mid-journey back to Marrakech). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or kasbah hotel. Relax and enjoy the dramatic gorge scenery at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — Moroccan bread, olive oil, jam, eggs, mint tea
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Skoura or Boumalne — kefta tagine or grilled chicken, budget 80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Kasbah guesthouse dinner or local restaurant in Dadès Valley — Berber lamb tagine, budget 100–180 MAD

day_by_day.notes: March mornings in the Sahara can be chilly — bring a warm layer for the sunrise. The Dadès Gorge road (Route des Mille Kasbahs) is scenic but winding; if prone to motion sickness, take medication. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the spectacular Dadès Gorge on a short morning hike along the canyon walls (1.5–2 hours, free). The dramatic rock formations known as 'Monkey Fingers' are a highlight. Return to your guesthouse for breakfast if not already taken, then depart for Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey to Marrakech, stop at the Kelaat M'Gouna Rose Valley (famous for its Damask rose fields — in March the buds are forming, with full bloom in April/May). Visit a local cooperative to see rose water and oil production. Continue driving through the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka pass, arriving in Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and spend a relaxed final Marrakech evening exploring the Gueliz (New City) neighborhood — browse contemporary art galleries, modern cafés, and upscale boutiques on Avenue Mohammed V.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Dadès Valley — Moroccan spread with msemen and honey
meals.lunch: Roadside café in Rose Valley or packed lunch — budget 60–100 MAD
meals.dinner: Gueliz restaurant — try Grand Café de la Poste or Café du Livre for a relaxed mid-range dinner, budget 150–220 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Dadès to Marrakech is approximately 4.5–5.5 hours. Depart by 9:00–10:00 AM to have a comfortable afternoon. If you have a private driver, negotiate the full multi-day rate upfront (typically 2,500–4,000 MAD for a 3-day desert circuit).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD including the Berber Museum) — a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Arrive at opening (8:00 AM) to enjoy it before crowds arrive. Stroll through vivid cobalt-blue buildings and exotic plant collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the Medina souks — pick up argan oil, Moroccan spices, leather goods, or handmade ceramics. Visit the Ensemble Artisanal (fixed-price government craft center) for fair-priced authentic souvenirs without bargaining pressure. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a final full Moroccan breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Yacout or Terrasse des Épices near the Medina — light lunch with Moroccan salads and pastilla, budget 120–180 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or an early dinner near the hotel before transfer — budget 100–150 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is very popular — booking tickets online in advance is strongly recommended (available on the official website). Keep some MAD for tips, final taxi rides, and airport purchases. Check your airline's baggage policy if you've purchased souvenirs — Moroccan crafts can add significant weight to luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer in a chauffeured Mercedes S-Class awaits. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy a welcome amenity — traditional mint tea, rose water hand wash, and a light charcuterie board prepared by the in-house chef. Unwind with a brief tour of your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In flight
meals.dinner: Late-night private in-room dining: Moroccan mezze platter with harira soup, briouats, and seasonal fruit, paired with fresh-squeezed orange juice or a glass of Moroccan rosé wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — priority is rest after a long flight. Confirm next-day activities and excursions with the resort concierge upon arrival. Luggage will be handled by the butler service.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, embark on a private guided walking tour of the UNESCO-listed Marrakech Medina. Explore the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens, the historic Saadian Tombs, and the magnificent El Badi Palace. Your personal guide will provide deep historical context on the Saadian and Alaouite dynasties. Travel by private air-conditioned vehicle between sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the exquisite Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship. Afterward, explore the vibrant souks of the Medina — spices, leather, lanterns, and textiles — with your guide facilitating an authentic and pressure-free shopping experience. Stop at a master artisan's workshop for a private demonstration of traditional zellige tilework.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna square at sunset for a curated sensory experience — watch storytellers, musicians, and acrobats as dusk falls. Then retire to a premium restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort featuring fresh pastries, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh juices, and eggs prepared to order.
meals.lunch: Private rooftop lunch at a riad restaurant in the Medina — lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, Moroccan salads, and freshly baked khobz bread.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk, a celebrated fine-dining restaurant in a restored 18th-century caravanserai — expect dishes like pigeon pastilla, slow-cooked lamb mechoui, and orange blossom crème brûlée.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina. The souks can be crowded — your guide will help navigate. Dress modestly near religious sites. Tipping your guide is customary and appreciated.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – March 17, 2027 (Marrakech – Gardens, Hammam & Culinary Arts)
day_by_day.morning: Begin with a private visit to the Majorelle Garden, the iconic cobalt-blue botanical sanctuary co-owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the Berber Museum within the garden grounds. Then walk to the nearby Yves Saint Laurent Museum for an immersive exhibition on fashion, art, and Morocco's influence on one of history's great designers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a 3-hour luxury hammam and spa ritual at the resort or at a renowned riad spa such as La Sultana Spa. Enjoy a black soap scrub (kessa), rhassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and rose water steam session — a quintessential Moroccan wellness experience.
day_by_day.evening: Participate in a private Moroccan cooking class led by a master chef inside a traditional riad kitchen. Learn to prepare bastilla, preserved lemon chicken tagine, and chebakia (honey-sesame pastry). Dine on your own creations in a candlelit courtyard.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — avocado toast on msemen, fresh Medjool dates, honey, argan oil, and a Moroccan coffee or spiced mint tea.
meals.lunch: Light post-hammam lunch at the spa lounge — mezze spreads, cold pressed juices, and a chilled Moroccan lemonade with orange blossom water.
meals.dinner: Dine on your own cooking-class creations in a private riad courtyard setting, complemented by Moroccan wine and a dessert of fresh fruit with rosewater syrup.

day_by_day.notes: Book hammam and cooking class slots in advance through the concierge. The Majorelle Garden can get busy after 10am — aim to arrive at opening time (9:00am). Photography is permitted in most garden areas.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – March 18, 2027 (Journey to the Sahara – Atlas Mountains & Kasbahs)
day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the epic journey toward the Sahara Desert. Cross the breathtaking High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at panoramic viewpoints for photography and a thermos of Moroccan mint tea prepared by your driver-guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Draa Valley and visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — one of the world's most spectacular earthen ksar (fortified villages) and a famous film location (Gladiator, Game of Thrones). Enjoy a private guided tour of the ksar with a local Berber expert. Continue through the Valley of Roses and the ancient Tinghir Gorges (Todra Gorge) for a short scenic walk.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your luxury desert camp or premium kasbah hotel near Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes). Check in and enjoy sunset cocktails on the terrace as the Sahara sky transforms into a canvas of amber and crimson.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before departure — croissants, yogurt, fresh fruit, and coffee to go.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic kasbah restaurant en route — traditional Berber couscous with seven vegetables, fresh salads, and mint tea.
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at your luxury desert camp — a multi-course Moroccan feast featuring mechoui lamb, vegetable couscous, and Berber desserts under a sky blazing with stars.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — depart by 7:00am. Bring a light jacket for the mountain pass, which can be cool in March. Ensure camera batteries are fully charged for the Atlas and Aït Benhaddou.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – March 19, 2027 (Sahara Desert – Dunes, Camel Trek & Stargazing)
day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a private camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes to witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises over the Sahara. Your Berber guide will lead you to a prime dune crest. Enjoy hot mint tea and dates as the golden light floods the desert. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Choose from premium adventure activities: a private 4x4 dune bashing excursion with a professional driver, sandboarding on the great dunes, or a guided quad bike ride through the desert landscape. Alternatively, visit a nearby Berber nomad family for a cultural exchange and traditional tea ceremony. Rest during the hottest part of the afternoon in your luxury tent or suite.
day_by_day.evening: As sunset approaches, climb the dunes on foot or by camel for golden-hour photography. After nightfall, enjoy a private stargazing session with a portable telescope and an astronomer guide — the Sahara offers some of the darkest, clearest skies in the world. Gather around a desert campfire for traditional Gnawa music performed by local musicians.

meals.breakfast: Post-sunrise camp breakfast — Berber omelette, msemen with honey and amlou, fresh orange juice, and spiced coffee.
meals.lunch: Relaxed lunch at the camp — grilled kefta skewers, Moroccan salads, harira soup, and chilled watermelon.
meals.dinner: Private open-air dinner beside the dunes — slow-roasted mechoui lamb, saffron couscous, grilled vegetables, and traditional Moroccan pastries, accompanied by Berber percussion and candlelight.

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures in March can drop significantly after sunset in the desert — bring a warm layer or blanket. Wear closed shoes for dune climbing. Sandboarding equipment is provided by the camp. Hydration is essential throughout the day.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – March 20, 2027 (Return to Marrakech – Figuig Route & Relaxation)
day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final sunrise walk among the dunes before breakfast. Depart the desert camp and begin the scenic return journey toward Marrakech. Stop at the oasis town of Erfoud, known for its fossil markets and ancient Trilobite deposits — browse and select a unique geological souvenir. Visit a fossil artisan workshop for a private demonstration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Ziz Valley, a stunning palm-lined gorge stretching for miles. Stop at the Source Bleue de Meski — a natural spring oasis — for a brief walk and refreshment break. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back into the Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy the remainder of the afternoon at leisure by the pool or with an in-room spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Spend a relaxed final evening in Marrakech with a sunset rooftop aperitivo at the resort, followed by a premium dinner at one of Marrakech's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast — freshly baked Moroccan bread, cheese, olive oil, honey, eggs, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a well-regarded local restaurant in Erfoud — harira, tagine of the day, and fresh dates from the Ziz Valley.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout, a legendary Marrakchi palace restaurant — enjoy a royal Moroccan banquet in a setting of zellige tiles, candlelight, and fountains, with rooftop cocktails to begin the evening.

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 8 hours — depart the desert camp by 7:30am to arrive comfortably before dinner. Pack desert items separately to avoid sand in main luggage. Confirm resort check-in readiness before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning at the resort. Take a sunrise swim or a gentle yoga session on the beachfront terrace. After breakfast, embark on a curated final half-day experience: visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues, browse the upscale boutiques of Gueliz (Marrakech's modern art and design district) for premium Moroccan crafts, leather goods, and argan beauty products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a farewell spa treatment — a 60-minute argan oil relaxation massage to ease any travel fatigue. Enjoy a final poolside lunch before preparing for departure. Your private luxury transfer will be arranged to Marrakech Menara Airport with ample time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with unforgettable memories of the ancient Medina, the High Atlas, and the infinite Sahara. Airport farewell gift bag from the resort — Moroccan argan oil, spice blends, and rose water — prepared by the concierge team.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a full spread of Moroccan and continental options, freshly squeezed juice, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Poolside farewell lunch — grilled sea bass chermoula, Moroccan salad trio, chilled gazpacho, and a dessert of orange and cinnamon tart.
meals.dinner: Light airport dining or onboard, as departure time dictates. The concierge can arrange a premium departure lounge experience at Marrakech Menara Airport.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out is typically at 12:00 noon — request a late checkout (2:00–3:00pm) through the concierge if your flight allows. Confirm all souvenir purchases are within customs allowances. Keep a small amount of Moroccan dirhams for tips and last-minute purchases. Exchange remaining dirhams at the airport.
